exhibits.title: Spot Price
exhibits.statement: Solana (SOL) traded at $100.73 as of 2026-10-25 10:17:50 UTC, +0.14% over one hour and -0.65% over twenty-four hours.

exhibits.title: 24-Hour Trading Range
exhibits.statement: Over twenty-four hours the price ranged from $98.8100 to $102.63; spot sits at 50% of that range.

exhibits.title: Seven-Day Trend
exhibits.statement: Price is -2.22% over seven days. The 24-hour average ($101.40) is below the 72-hour average ($102.89). Spot is 7.22% below the seven-day high of $108.56 and 1.94% above the seven-day low of $98.8100.

exhibits.title: Volatility & Momentum
exhibits.statement: Realized volatility computed from hourly closes is 2.45% per day. The 14-hour relative strength index reads 45.3, conventionally neutral.

exhibits.title: Liquidity
exhibits.statement: Twenty-four-hour trading volume was $2.05 billion, equal to 3.44% of the $59.41 billion market capitalization.

exhibits.title: Market Sentiment
exhibits.statement: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index reads 54 ("Neutral"), versus 53 7 days earlier.

exhibits.title: Chainlink Price Feed
exhibits.statement: The Chainlink SOL/USD Data Feed on Ethereum mainnet last reported $101.99, 10.8 hours before the spot quote and +1.25% against the spot price in Exhibit A. Practice positions are entered and settled at this mark.

arguments.text:
May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price of SOL sits squarely at the midpoint of its 24‑hour range, indicating a balanced supply‑demand equilibrium that historically precedes modest upward drift as traders accumulate near the median price point [Ex. B].  

2. Realized volatility is modest at 2.45% per day and the RSI is neutral at 45.3, suggesting the market is not over‑extended and can sustain a bullish bias without triggering stop‑loss cascades [Ex. D].  

3. The Chainlink price feed, which governs settlement, is already 1.25% above the spot quote, providing an immediate upside buffer for a long practice position and aligning with a neutral‑to‑bullish sentiment reading of 54 on the Fear & Greed Index [Ex. F, G].  

The Bull rests.

May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price sits squarely at the midpoint of a tight 24‑hour range ($98.81‑$102.63) and has shown only a negligible 0.14% rise in the last hour, indicating a lack of directional pressure; the market’s neutral Fear & Greed reading of 54 reinforces this equilibrium (Ex. B, F).  

2. Realized volatility is modest at 2.45% per day and the RSI of 45.3 is firmly in neutral territory, suggesting that any price swing is likely to be contained and reversible rather than a breakout to the upside (Ex. D).  

3. Although the Chainlink feed posted $101.99, a 1.25% premium to the spot, this premium reflects a short‑lived arbitrage gap; the underlying liquidity of $2.05 B (3.44% of market cap) is sufficient to absorb the premium without sustaining a bullish bias (Ex. E, G).  

The Bear rests.

Your Honor, the Bear’s first point collapses under Exhibit C, which shows SOL trading 7.22 % below its seven‑day high and its 24‑hour average ($101.40) already beneath the 72‑hour average ($102.89), a clear bearish tilt that the “midpoint” argument ignores. Likewise, the second point relies on Exhibit D’s “neutral” RSI, yet the same data reveal a realized volatility of 2.45 % per day—still enough to erode the thin $4‑range and permit a breakout, especially when the price sits at the exact 50 % mark of that range (Exhibit B), a classic springboard for a move upward. Nothing further.

Your Honor, the Bull’s first premise collapses under Exhibit B: the price sits exactly at the 50 % point of a narrow $3.82 range, a condition that historically yields no directional bias; median‑price accumulation is a neutral phenomenon, not a bullish catalyst. Moreover, Exhibit C shows a seven‑day downtrend (‑2.22 %) and a 24‑hour average ($101.40) below the 72‑hour average ($102.89), evidencing persistent weakness that the midpoint argument ignores.  

Second, the Bull’s volatility‑RSI argument ignores the momentum context: Exhibit D’s RSI of 45.3 is below the bullish threshold of 50, indicating slight bearish pressure, while the modest 2.45 % daily volatility simply reflects a tranquil market lacking the impetus for an upward swing.  

Nothing further.

ruling.holding: The Court finds a short practice position is warranted.

findings.finding: Seven‑day price is down 2.22% and 24‑hour average lies below the 72‑hour average, indicating bearish momentum.
RSI at 45.3 is below the bullish threshold and volatility is modest, suggesting limited upward impetus.
Fear & Greed Index reads 54 (Neutral), offering no bullish sentiment support.

ruling.opinion: Exhibit C shows SOL trading below recent averages, a clear bearish tilt. Exhibit D’s RSI under 50 and low volatility signal insufficient bullish force. Neutral sentiment in Exhibit F adds no upside catalyst. Together these factors outweigh the midpoint range argument, leading to a short expectation for the next 24 hours.
ruling.dissent: The Bull argues the mid‑range price and Chainlink premium signal upside, but the prevailing downtrend and neutral momentum in the exhibits outweigh that claim.
